(2) FIRST cross-module-type circuit: question = 5 heads {10.5,12.6,15.6,15.1,9.7} + rank-2 mlp11 slice, 99.4% additive, slice marginal .166 at zero added global cost (S1576). _slice_writer_graph.standing_statement: S1600-1603: heads 9.7/10.5 + mlp9/mlp10 write '?' evidence into span(v1,v2), which IS the '?' unembedding direction (logit-lens rank 1). The channel accumulates MONOTONICALLY across the whole stack with no front/middle reversal, peaking at attn16 (6/6); mlp11 is the largest single positive step (+1028) but only ~69% of the peak is reached by then. Suppression is MLP-only and late: mlp16 (-292) and mlp17 (-1151, largest of any sign) cut it back by .358 +/- .029 while attn17 still writes positively (+139). The late-peak SHAPE is general (12/12, two classes, two sites) but the READ-WRITE relationship is NOT: mlp11 amplifies the channel it reads (+1028) while mlp17 opposes its own payload (-1374 to -5111), so any 'module X reads and writes the same variable' claim needs testing per site (S1604). No small component set reproduces the final cut (top-4 positive = .414) because the quantity is assembled by ~34 positive steps against 2 large negative ones.

pronouns_depth_profile.in_flight: readwrite_2x2: {question,pronouns} x {mlp11,mlp17} under one uniform slice rule, to identify whether SITE or CLASS decides the read-write sign (S1601 and S1604 differ in both, so neither is identified).

readwrite_2x2.design: {question,pronouns} x {mlp11,mlp17}, one uniform pos_r8 payload rule, 3 disjoint samples per cell; recon rel err 6.3e-08 to 3.6e-07
readwrite_2x2.finding: THE SELF-WRITE SIGN TRACKS THE CLASS, NOT THE SITE. Question writes INTO its payload directions at both sites (6/6 samples); pronouns writes AGAINST its own at both (6/6). The S1601-vs-S1604 contrast previously attributed to depth is a class difference. The driver's site hypothesis was exactly inverted and all three registered bars FAILED.
readwrite_2x2.instrument_limit: TWO OF FOUR CELLS ARE DEGENERATE AND THEIR DEPTH CURVES MUST NOT BE USED: question@mlp17 peaks at layers 1-2 with drawdowns nan/nan/35.85 (curve never rises, ratio divides by ~0); pronouns@mlp11 peaks at the TERMINAL component so drawdown is exactly 0.000 by construction. Both are OFF-SITE cells. The depth-curve method yields a coherent accumulation profile ONLY at a class's own certified site. Self-write is a signed sum with no division and stays valid everywhere, which is why the class-not-site conclusion survives while cross-cell drawdown/peak comparisons do not.
readwrite_2x2.do_not_use: the |mlp17|/|mlp11| ratios (.771 question, 17.11 pronouns) -- question's numerator comes from a degenerate curve

writer_floor_control.finding: A RANDOM rank-8 subspace has 'writers': consensus top-6 mlp17, mlp16, mlp15, attn16, attn17, attn13. Component attribution onto ANY low-rank subspace is dominated by the largest-output-norm components. All three real slice rules at pronouns@mlp17 share exactly {mlp17, mlp16, mlp15} with the random control.
writer_floor_control.floor_corrected: raw Jaccard(|lambda|-rule, payload-rule) = .333; FLOOR-CORRECTED = .000 -- the entire apparent agreement between two slice rules was the floor. Rule-specific tails are disjoint: |lambda| picks x0/attn12/mlp9, payload picks mlp11/mlp12/mlp13, gate picks mlp14/x0/attn12.
writer_floor_control.passed: Jaccard(|lambda|, gate) .714 > Jaccard(|lambda|, payload) .333 -- the |lambda| slice at a suppression-dominated site is gate-dominated (S1598's own lesson, confirmed from the other side).
writer_floor_control.standing_requirement: EVERY component-level writer/attribution claim needs a random-subspace control at matched rank; only the floor-corrected set may be named as writers. LESSONS 15.

head_grain_control.verdict: THE HEAD-GRAIN LAW SURVIVES. |lambda| slice vs matched-rank random, 3 disjoint samples per arm, both published cells.
head_grain_control.published_ratios_reproduce: S1598 attn9 6.8:1 -> 6.93 measured; S1598 attn12 9.1:1 -> 8.45; S1597 attn10 20:1 -> 33.15 (exceeds). Fresh disjoint rows, no refitting.
head_grain_control.negative_control_inside: question@mlp9: |lambda| head 9.7 at 1.11 vs random 1.16 = 1.0x separation, NO concentration -- and S1597 never claimed a sharp head there (attn9 slice writing 221 vs attn10's 625). The law holds where the writer graph says the circuit is and is SILENT where it is not; that asymmetry is what distinguishes mechanism from norm artifact.
head_grain_control.pred_c_failed: whole-stack median beats random by only 1.165x/1.395x vs a 1.5x bar. MEASUREMENT lesson, not physics: the law is layer-specific, so a median over 18 layers averages an 18.8x effect at one layer into noise from ~16 with no class signal. The registered statistic could not detect what it was registered for.

component_floor_control_question.CORRECTION_S1611: STATISTIC MISMATCH, found 2026-08-27 06:45. This harness ranks components by POSITIVE-ONLY signed contribution; S1597 (slice_writers.py:216) and S1598 (slice_writers_p.py:205) both rank by ABSOLUTE attribution mass (.abs().sum()). Different statistic, ranking and denominator. The headline 'random .7223 is indistinguishable from S1597's .718' compares two DIFFERENT quantities and is WITHDRAWN -- the closeness is coincidence. null_share_is_not_tabulable.question: can the matched-rank null share be tabulated from (rank, TOP) and reused, or does every claim need its own random arm?
null_share_is_not_tabulable.answer: EVERY CLAIM NEEDS ITS OWN MATCHED-CLASS, MATCHED-RANK ARM. The class effect (.1417) is 3.3x the rank effect (.0427), so the dominant term changes with every claim.
null_share_is_not_tabulable.self_consistency: the question rank-2 null reproduced S1612's .4489 to four decimals -- the harness is sound, so the two failures are real
null_share_is_not_tabulable.n_hypothesis_NOT_supported: the null loosely tracks class count (question n=102 lowest, 'the' n=2354 highest) but Spearman rho = .800 on N=4 with exact permutation p = .167; 'is' (519) and 'pronouns' (399) invert the ordering. UNDERPOWERED, not supported. Needs ~7+ classes.
null_share_is_not_tabulable.CONSTRAINS_S1612: the pronouns-vs-question null gap (.7295 vs .4489) confounds rank, TOP and class together. S1612's WITHIN-cell conclusions stand (each slice vs its own null on identical rows), but nothing licenses comparing the two cells' shares -- and by the same logic S1598's .482 must NOT be set against S1597's .718.

null_share_mechanism_is_not_n.powered_result: rho(class n, null share) = .6727 at permutation p = .0192 over 10 classes spanning n=118 to 6911. S1613's underpowered association (rho .800, p .167 on 4 classes) is REAL at power.
null_share_mechanism_is_not_n.but_n_is_NOT_the_mechanism: equalising every class to a common 117 class positions removes only 6.1% of the spread (.1780 -> .1672), and the class ORDERING survives at rank correlation .952 -- 'said' lowest in both, 'the' highest in both.
null_share_mechanism_is_not_n.control_validity: the n-controlled range (.1672) stays far above the .01 floor, so subsampling did not destroy the measurement -- this distinguishes 'n is not the cause' from 'the control broke the instrument'.
null_share_mechanism_is_not_n.PRACTICAL_RULE: a matched-CLASS random arm is mandatory and CANNOT be substituted by matching n. The null cannot be tabulated from (rank, TOP) (S1613) and cannot be normalised away by equalising sample size (S1614). Every writer-graph claim carries its own arm at its own class.
null_share_mechanism_is_not_n.bookkeeping: S1613's printed class counts were the LAST CHUNK's, not totals (question n=102 there vs 334 total). The two sets of n figures must not be read against each other; S1613's conclusions are unaffected as its comparisons were within-run.
null_share_mechanism_is_not_n.open: what property of a class's POSITIONS sets its null -- position-in-sequence distribution, document concentration, or local context entropy. n is a correlate of that property, not the cause.
null_share_mechanism_is_not_n.WITHDRAWN_BY_S1616: THE POWERED RESULT DOES NOT GENERALISE. This entry recorded rho(class n, null share) = .6727 at p = .0192 as 'REAL at power'. On 10 DISJOINT classes (S1616, verified zero overlap, n range 115-7394) the same measurement gives rho = .0182 at p = .9601. The association was a property of that particular 10-class set, not of the method. The powered_result claim is WITHDRAWN.
null_share_mechanism_is_not_n.what_survives: the NEGATIVE finding, which never depended on the correlation: equalising every class to a common 117 positions removes only 6.1% of the class spread and the class ordering survives at rank rho .952. n is not the mechanism -- that stands. What is withdrawn is that n is even a reliable CORRELATE.

nothing_predicts_the_null.summary: after five sections and four failed hypotheses, NOTHING predicts the null share: not n (S1614, withdrawn), not position or document structure (S1614n), not deviation magnitude (S1615), not signal-to-noise (S1616). S1613's core claim is unaffected -- it rests on the OBSERVED spread, not on any predictor.
nothing_predicts_the_null.THE_ONE_LAW_THAT_HOLDS: the estimation-NOISE floor scales as 1/sqrt(n) at rho .988-1.000 across two DISJOINT 10-class sets. It is a property of the noise, not the signal -- and it came from the CONTROL ARM of a failed experiment, not from any hypothesis.
nothing_predicts_the_null.METHODOLOGICAL_WARNING: a post-hoc candidate chosen from four options on 10 points reached rho .733 at p .020 and evaporated to .079 on fresh classes; a correlation that PASSED a registered bar at p .019 collapsed to .018. ON N=10 WITH FREELY CHOSEN PREDICTORS, p < .05 CARRIES ALMOST NO INFORMATION. Every correlational claim in this program on ~10 units needs a disjoint confirmatory set before it is quoted.
nothing_predicts_the_null.bar_design_flaw_recorded: S1616's pred_b ('SNR beats n') PASSED vacuously -- |.0788| > |.0182| is true while both are indistinguishable from zero. A comparative bar without an absolute floor can be satisfied by two null quantities. Scored as a pass because it was registered that way, and flagged.

head_grain_generality.what_was_tested: S1608 certified the head-grain law on TWO cells at 3.1-18.8x separation. S1617 tests GENERALITY: 6 new classes (colon, months, close_paren, digits, comma, and) x both mlp11 and mlp17 x their certified layers = 30 cells, |lambda|-r8 vs matched-rank random on identical rows.
head_grain_generality.HEAD_GRAIN_FLOOR: in 4 of the 12 lambda hits the RANDOM arm finds the SAME certified head (close_paren L13 both sites, 'and' L10 both sites) -- at those layers the certified head dominates under ANY basis. GENUINE DISCRIMINATION IS 8/30 = 26.7%, not 40%. The S1606 floor reaches head grain too; S1608 found none only because its two cells happened not to have it.
head_grain_generality.digits_is_instructive: the |lambda| top head is a consistent NEIGHBOUR of the certified head at every layer -- 7.8 vs 7.3, 6.7 vs 6.5, 12.7 vs 12.6, 11.6 vs 11.5. The slice resolves to a nearby but different head, not to noise. comma and 'and' show exact hits elsewhere, so this is not an indexing artifact.
head_grain_generality.site_effect: mlp17 46.7% vs mlp11 33.3% -- consistent with mlp17 as the late readout. Testing both rather than guessing one avoided understating the law by a third.
head_grain_generality.REVISES_THE_UNIVERSAL_CLAIM: S1597/S1598's 'EVERY attention writer of a certified eigen slice resolves at head grain to a certified circuit head of that class' is TOO STRONG as a general statement. Supported form: at SOME classes and sites the slice resolves to the certified head, at ~3x a matched-rank random basis and ~27% absolute after floor correction; at others (digits, months) it resolves to a NEIGHBOURING head. S1608 stands as written for its own two cells.
head_grain_generality.S1618_mechanism: the digits 0/8 failure is EXPLAINED: the slice picks high-norm generalists (selectivity 0.10-1.20) over the certified specialists (6.7-11.2), confirmed by causal removal. Where attribution and removal DISAGREE, prefer removal -- causal won 3/4 on rise and 3/4 on selectivity, with the losses concentrated where selectivity was tied.

_priority_metric_validation.claim: SUPERSEDED -- see CORRECTED_2026-08-27. Retained verbatim above so the error and its correction are both legible.
_priority_metric_validation.evidence: Codex's ship_error_factorial (token-cell factorial over {attention, mlp012, deep}, 480 rows/split, discovery skip=7000 + heldout skip=11000) finds mlp012 the DOMINANT group in 6/6 token cells on BOTH splits. Exact weighted Shapley on heldout: attention -0.0670, MLP0-2 +0.7277, deep MLPs +0.2120, summing to 0.8727 = the full ship exactly.
_priority_metric_validation.convergence: priorities.md ranks mlp1 (.181), mlp0 (.062), mlp2 (.041) as targets 1-3 -- i.e. exactly mlp012. Two instruments built on different principles (per-component substitution fidelity vs group factorial ablation) return the same answer: the early MLPs own the remaining error.
_priority_metric_validation.caution_that_came_with_it: group effects are NOT additive and NOT monotone -- attention's Shapley effect is NEGATIVE (-0.0670), and ablating attention on top of mlp012+deep REDUCES damage by 9-29% in 6/6 cells (S1334 inversion). Consequence: any bill that SUMS per-group substitution costs overstates the total by ~33% (ALL3/sum-of-singles = .664-.772). Frontier entries must not be priced group-wise.
_priority_metric_validation.CORRECTED_2026-08-27: The original claim of 'INDEPENDENT confirmation' was TOO STRONG and is withdrawn. Codex's math red-team (board 05:24) is right on the decisive point: SHAPLEY CLOSURE IS AN IDENTITY, not evidence. Shapley values sum to the grand-coalition value by the efficiency axiom, so '-0.0670 + 0.7277 + 0.2120 = 0.8727' is arithmetic and I should not have cited it as part of the evidence.
_priority_metric_validation.independence_reassessed: Beyond Codex's point: the two instruments are not independent either. priorities.md ranks by delta_opt x (1 - best fidelity) -- the residual CE cost of substituting a component -- and the factorial measures the CE cost of substituting the deployed planks for a group. Those are close to the SAME quantity computed per-component vs per-group. Worse, the ship's planks were BUILT by targeting the priority board, so mlp012 carrying the residual error is partly a construction artifact: Codex notes the early planks were fit under the attention composite and the bundle includes incumbent MLP2 glue.
_priority_metric_validation.what_the_agreement_DOES_show: a coherence check, not a validation: per-component unexplained-CE estimates aggregate to the right group ranking EVEN THOUGH group effects are non-additive and one is negative. That is mildly informative about the aggregation, and nothing more. The priority metric remains WITHOUT an independent validation.
_priority_metric_validation.provisional_data: Codex's red-team also found factorial v1 bugs: the copy mask covers distances 2-65 rather than 1-64, and rare vocabularies were recomputed per split. TOKEN-CELL values (copy / novel_freq / novel_rare) are therefore PROVISIONAL. The global MLP0-2 allocation 0.7277 / 0.8727 is unaffected. The non-additivity and negative-attention findings rest on the global numbers and on the m+d vs ALL3 contrast, which survive; but any per-cell number quoted from S1608-era boards should be treated as provisional.
